verses.1: Having spoken thus to Rama and praised him repeatedly, Rama, the delight of the Raghus, then spoke another statement.
verses.2: O best among men, take these four thousand horses, two thousand chariots, and a hundred excellent elephants.
verses.3: Let market streets adorned with various goods, and similarly actors and dancers, follow Kakutstha along the way.
verses.4: O Shatrughna, best among men, take a million units of gold and fine gold, and go, equipped with ample wealth and conveyances.
verses.5: O hero, O best among men, please the well-maintained, cheerful, well-nourished, and disciplined army by engaging in good conversation and bestowing gifts.
verses.6: O Raghava, neither wealth, wives, nor relatives truly endure, but a well-pleased retinue will remain with you wherever you are.
verses.7: Then, having dispatched a great army filled with joyful people, you alone, holding a bow in hand, should go to the forest of Madhu.
verses.8: You should go without suspicion, so that Lavana, the son of Madhu, does not recognize you as one going and desiring battle.
verses.9: O best among men, there is no other way to kill him, for anyone who approaches his sight is indeed slain by Lavana.
verses.10: O gentle one, you should kill Lavana when summer has departed and the rainy season has arrived, for that is indeed the opportune time for that wicked one.
verses.11: Let your soldiers proceed, placing the great sages in front, so that they may cross the waters of the Ganga with the remaining part of summer.
verses.12: Having stationed your entire army on the river bank, you, swift in action, should proceed ahead with your bow.
verses.13: Thus addressed by Rama, Shatrughna gathered those mighty army chiefs and then spoke these words.
verses.14: These are your assigned camps where you shall dwell, and you must stay peacefully so that no one is troubled.
verses.15: Having thus instructed them and sent forth the great army, he then saluted Kausalya, Sumitra, and Kaikeyi.
verses.16: Having circumambulated Rama and bowed down with his head, Shatrughna, the tormentor of enemies, was then given leave by Rama.
verses.17: The mighty and pure-minded Shatrughna, having bowed down with folded hands to Lakshmana, Bharata, and the priest Vasishtha, and having performed circumambulation, then departed.
verses.18: Having first sent forth his army, which was crowded with excellent elephants and horses, Shatrughna, the增ifier of the Raghu dynasty, then stayed by the king's side for a month before departing. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे चतुष्षष्टितमः सर्गः ।। 64 ।। Thus ends the sixty-fourth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
